work.tagline: A university e-learning platform built for scale.
work.headline: Built an e-learning platform that changed how students study.
work.description: SoliQuiz is a full-stack pedagogical platform for university students and professors. Features a QCM builder, role-based dashboards (Admin, Prof, Student), real-time quiz sessions, and a rich analytics module. The entire UI was designed with a custom 'Luminous' design system built in Alpine.js and Laravel Blade.

sections.title: The challenge
sections.body: University students had no centralized platform to practice QCMs, track their progress, or interact with professors. Professors had to manage evaluations manually, leading to inefficiencies and poor analytics. The platform needed to serve three distinct user roles — Admin, Professor, and Student — each with completely different needs, workflows, and permissions.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: I designed a modular role-based architecture from the ground up. The backend leverages Laravel's Eloquent ORM and a clean RESTful API. The frontend was built with Alpine.js for lightweight reactivity within Blade templates, keeping the stack cohesive and fast without over-engineering. A custom Luminous design system ensured visual consistency across all 30+ views.

sections.title: What I built
sections.body: A QCM builder that lets professors create question banks and link them to evaluations. A real-time quiz engine for students. A full Admin dashboard for user management, audit logs, and system configuration. An analytics module showing per-student, per-evaluation, and per-course metrics. Full multilingual support with French and Arabic.

work.tagline: International real estate, 4 languages, one platform.
work.headline: A multilingual real estate site built for global reach.
work.description: Warden Properties is an international real estate marketing website targeting buyers in Morocco, Spain, the UK, and the Gulf. The project required a 4-language architecture (EN, FR, ES, AR) with right-to-left support, a complete SEO strategy using hreflang/canonical tags, and a conversion-focused UI deployed on Vercel.

sections.title: The challenge
sections.body: Real estate clients browse in their native language and search engines must serve the right language version. A single misconfigured hreflang can tank rankings across markets. The site also needed to handle Arabic RTL layout without a framework — pure, clean HTML and CSS.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: Each language lives in its own directory (/en, /fr, /es, /ar), sharing assets but with fully translated content. Canonical URLs were standardized to avoid duplicate content penalties. hreflang tags were audited across all pages. The CSS uses logical properties to support both LTR and RTL layouts from a single stylesheet.

sections.title: Results
sections.body: The site achieved first-page rankings across all four target markets within 3 months of launch. Load times under 1.2s on mobile. Vercel's edge network ensures sub-100ms TTFB globally. The client expanded their ad spend by 3x after seeing the organic growth.

work.tagline: Built from scratch with React, Vite, and Tailwind.
work.headline: Designed and built entirely with React. No templates.
work.description: This portfolio was built from scratch — every layout decision, interaction, and detail is intentional. Inspired by editorial design, it prioritizes readability and craft over flashy effects. Built with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, and react-router-dom.

sections.title: Why build it
sections.body: I wanted a portfolio that felt like mine — not a theme, not a template. Every spacing decision, every font weight, every color was chosen deliberately. The reference was Anukul Gurung's portfolio, which I admire for its editorial clarity and typographic discipline.
